source_edition: CC0 1.0 English translation from the modern Amharic EOTC text, Internet Archive item three-books-of-meqabyan-cc0-translation (2026). Not from Ge'ez. Provisional: weigh below KJV, WEB, and Charles.

1.text: This is the book that tells how Maqabis found the Jews in Syria between the two rivers; how, from the Jabbok all the way to the square of Jerusalem, he slaughtered them in their valleys; and how he destroyed the holy city.

2.text: From Samaria as far as the square of Jerusalem, even to all her districts they encamped; with the sword they killed, leaving few survivors. For the Edomites and the Syrians and the Amalekites had made common cause with Maqabis the man of Moab, the destroyer of the city of Jerusalem.

3.text: When the sons of Israel transgressed, [God] raised against them Maqabis the Moabite; and he killed them all with the sword.

4.text: Therefore the enemies of God grew arrogant against the holy city; in their iniquity they made common cause.

5.text: Edomites and Philistines also encamped [there]; for he [God] had sent them, since they had challenged the word of God; they began to take vengeance on the city of God.

6.text: That Maqabis’s country was Remat of Moab; with strength he arose from his country, and with all the men who were with him he made common cause.

7.text: That they might destroy the city of God, they encamped in Mesopotamia and the valleys of Galaboh as far as Syria; there he sought out the Philistines and the Amalekites; and he gave them much gold and silver, horses and chariots, that they might be one with him in iniquity.

8.text: And coming together, they overthrew her fortress; the inhabitants of her shed blood like water.

9.text: They made Jerusalem like the hut of a vineyard-keeper; they raised a din within her; he [Maqabis] did every wicked work that God does not love; they defiled the city of God which was full of righteousness and holiness.

10.text: “They made the corpses of your servants food for the birds of heaven. They made the flesh of your righteous ones food for the wild beasts of the desert.”

11.text: They plundered widows and orphans; what Satan had taught them, they did, without fearing God; until God who searches the kidneys and the heart became angry, they ripped out the fetuses in the wombs of pregnant women.

12.text: Because they had done evil to the people of God, they returned to their country rejoicing; they took the plunder they had captured from the holy city.

13.text: And when they returned and entered their houses, they made joy, song, and clapping.

1.text: The prophet whom they call Re’ay said to him: “Be glad a little today, while it is yet morning; for the Holy One of Israel, the LORD, shall avenge himself against you with a scourge you did not expect.

2.text: “Will you say, ‘Horses are swift, therefore by running I will escape’?

3.text: “I say to you: the men who pursue you are swifter than carrion-birds; from destruction and the wrath of God which comes upon you, you shall not escape.

4.text: “Will you say, ‘I will put on armor of iron; the casting of spears and the shooting of arrows cannot touch me’? The Holy One of Israel, the LORD, says: ‘It is not by the casting of spears that I will avenge myself against you’; but worse than the casting of spears and the shooting of arrows, I will bring upon you grievous heart-disease, eczema, and gout.

5.text: “For you have stirred my anger; I will bring heart-disease upon you; you shall lack a helper; until I have destroyed the calling of your name from the earth, you shall not escape my hand.

6.text: “Because you have stiffened your neck, because you have exalted your head over my city — when in the blink of an eye I do this thing swiftly, you shall know that I, the LORD, am your Creator. For before me you are like grass before the wind which fire devours; before me you are like dust which the whirlwind takes from the earth and scatters.

7.text: “You have stirred my anger; you have not known your Creator. I will disregard all that is yours; in every fortress of yours that takes refuge, I will leave nothing.

8.text: “Now turn from all the wickedness you have done. If you turn — if you confess before God utterly with weeping and sorrow, if you petition him with a pure heart — God will forgive you all the sin you have committed before him.”

9.text: Then Maqabis, clothed in dust, wept before God for his sin; for God had been angry with him.

10.text: And he knew that God would not delay the scourge the prophet had spoken in God’s name. For God’s eyes are open and he does not sleep; his ears are open and he does not disregard; the word he has spoken he does not make false; in one blink of an eye he does it swiftly.

11.text: He cast off his garments and put on sackcloth; he scattered dust on his head; for the wickedness he had done, he cried out before his Creator God; he wept.

1.text: Remat of Moab is near Syria; the prophet spoke to him.

2.text: He dug a pit and entered it up to his neck; he wept a bitter weeping; he repented before God for the sin he had committed.

3.text: And God said to the prophet: “Return from the land of Judah to Remat, to Maqabis the chief of Moab. Say to him: God says thus: ’It was I, the LORD your Creator, who in my will sent you that you might destroy my city — not lest you say,”By my own might and the firmness of my army I destroyed the holy city.” It was not you who did this thing;

4.text: “for in all her covetousness, in her denial and her lechery, she grieved me.

5.text: “And I disregarded her; into your hand I delivered her. Not for your sake, lest you stiffen your neck and say,”I encompassed the city with the strength of my own hand.” But now, for the sake of the children whom you have begotten, God forgives you your sin.

6.text: “Now, with all your heart, take courage and repent. Those who waver do not take courage to repent; do not be a waverer.

7.text: “But those who repent with all their mind, who in everything they have repented of do not return to perversity and sin — they are blessed.

8.text: “And those who take courage, with weeping and sorrow, with much petition and prostration, to return to their Creator God — they are blessed. For he has said: ‘You who have repented after you erred — you who have repented are mine.’

9.text: “To the proud one who has erred — when he has turned back in repentance — he says: ‘For your fear and your terror, I forgive you your sin.’ For I am the LORD your Creator, who bring the sin of the father upon the children to the third and fourth generation, but to those who love me and keep my law, I show mercy to the thousandth generation. [Ex 20:5–6 / Deut 5:9–10]

10.text: “Now, for the children you have begotten, I will keep my covenant with you; for the sin you have done, I will accept the repentance you have made — so says God Almighty, the Holy One of Israel.’”

11.text: Then he came up out of the pit, saying: “I have grieved God! Do as you please to me; but let me not be separated from you. May God do thus and more to me!” — and he prostrated himself before the prophet. “We had no law; we did not walk in his commandments as our fathers did; as our fathers taught us, we worshiped the idol; you know.

12.text: “I am a sinner who has walked in my sin and the pride of my heart; in the stiffness of my neck I have grieved my Creator. Until now I have not heard the words of God’s prophets; in his law and commandments which he commanded me, I have not lived.”

13.text: And the prophet answered: “Before you, no one from your people has confessed his sin; today I have known that he has accepted your repentance.”

14.text: “From now on, leave off worshiping idols; turn to the knowledge of God, that your conversion may be true.” And he prostrated himself at the prophet’s feet; the prophet raised him; he commanded him all the good works that were fitting.

15.text: And he did as God had commanded; he returned to his house.

16.text: That Maqabis put his mind in order. From his house he removed the idol and the divination, the idol-worshipers and the diviners, the sorcerers.

17.text: And the children he had brought from Jerusalem as captives — morning and evening he examined them, whether, as their fathers used to do, they kept all the commandments of God, his ordinances and his law.

18.text: From the captive children, from the educated, he appointed [them] over his house.

19.text: Furthermore — that they might teach his small, well-loved younger children all that the sons of Israel do (the law of God) — he appointed educated ones from among the smaller [captives] to enter his bedchamber; he heard from the captive children all the ordinances of God, his worship and judgment, and all the customs the Moabites practiced.

20.text: Their shrines, their divinations and their idols, the kid-goats and ewe-lambs they fattened morning and evening, the sacrifice and wine they offered to the idols — these he destroyed.

21.text: At noon and at every hour, in all his work, he used to bow and worship them [the idols]; he used to petition them and trust them; even on returning from a journey, he used to petition them; the priests of the idols, in everything they told him, he used to do their will.

22.text: It seemed to him that in everything they saved him; therefore he did not despise anything they spoke.

1.text: There was a time he saved them by Joshua.

2.text: There was a time he saved them by Gideon.

3.text: There was a time he saved them by Samson, by Barak and Deborah, and by Judith; for, whether through woman or man, dwelling in [the deliverer] — he raised judges to save them from the hand of the enemies who tortured them.

4.text: And God, as he willed, used to save them from the hand of those who tortured them.

5.text: In all the good he did for them — by multiplying the seed of their land, all the flock of their wilderness, and their cattle — he gladdened them.

6.text: He used to bless their cattle and their plantings; in house and in wilderness, all they took hold of he used to bless; he looked upon them with the eye of mercy; he did not diminish their livestock; for they were the children of the righteous, and he loved them utterly.

7.text: But when they did evil in their work, into the hand of their enemies he delivered them up.

8.text: When he destroyed them, at once they sought him; turning back, they ran to their Creator God.

9.text: When they turned with their whole mind, he forgave their sin. For he knows they are flesh and blood; the deceiving thought of this world and the demons are upon them; their former sin he did not remember against them.

10.text: Now that Maqabis, when he heard this ordinance which God had made on the holy mountain, strove in repentance.

11.text: After he had seen this thing and heard it, he did not slacken in doing good works. Because God had forgiven them, he did not slacken in doing all the kindness the sons of Israel do; when they transgressed his commandment, when God scourged them — they wept and cried out; and again he forgave them; they kept his law.

12.text: And Maqabis made his way straight likewise; he kept his commandment; he walked in the commandment of the LORD God of Israel.

13.text: Then, hearing all those in whom the sons of Israel trusted, he came to trust as they did — by keeping the commandment of God.

14.text: His house and his children he urged to walk in all the law and commandment of God.

15.text: What the Jews were forbidden by ordinance, he too forbade himself; the commandment the Jews kept, he heard and kept. Though he was of distinct Moabite stock, he refrained from the foods the Jews were forbidden.

16.text: He set aside the tithe; from his sheep and his cows, from his donkeys, the firstborn and all he had purchased he used to give; even as the Jews offered sacrifice, with his face turned toward Jerusalem, he offered sacrifice.

17.text: The sacrifice of his vow and of his sin, of his will and of his peace, and the perpetual sacrifice — he offered.

18.text: He gave the first of his harvest; the wine-offering the Jews offered, he too offered; he gave it to the Levite he had appointed; all that the Jews did, he did likewise; he made the incense fragrant.

19.text: Candlesticks and vessels, tables and tent-curtains, the four colors and rings, the pure oil for the lampstand of the Holy of Holies — when Israel served God in the Holy of Holies — and the curtain, he had made.

20.text: When [the Jews] lived in his law and ordinance, when God did not disregard them and deliver them into the hand of their enemies — Maqabis also did good works in all his ways.

21.text: That [God] might be a leader to him, that he might not separate him from the people of Israel whom he had chosen and whose will he did — he always prayed to the Creator of Israel.

22.text: That he might be given a son in Zion, a house in Jerusalem, and that he might be saved from the destruction the prophet had spoken — that all his repentance and the weeping he had wept before God might be received as his repentance —

23.text: that his seed might not be destroyed from the earth, that he might be kept in his going-out and his coming-in — he prayed again.

24.text: The Moabite peoples under Maqabis’s authority were pleased to believe; for their chief walked in a straight way, and they saw his judgment; they did his will; for they had despised the judgment and the language of their own country, and they observed that Maqabis’s work was straight and better.

25.text: And they came to him; they heard the mercy and the true judgment of Maqabis.

26.text: He had much wealth: male servants and female servants, camels and donkeys; he had five hundred armored horses; he utterly defeated the Philistines, the Amalekites, and the Syrians — whereas formerly, when he had worshiped idols, they had defeated him.

27.text: But since he had trusted in God, when he went out to battle, it was he who won; there was none who could defeat him.

28.text: They came against him in the strength of their idols to attack him; in the name of their idols they cursed him; but because he had placed his faith on his Creator God, there was none who could defeat him.

29.text: Doing this, and defeating his enemies, and ruling the heathen by his authority — he lived.

30.text: For the wronged he used to avenge; he used to vindicate the cause of the orphan.

31.text: Widows and orphans in their time of need he used to receive; the hungry he satisfied from his food; the naked he clothed from his garments.

32.text: In his wisdom and in the work of his hand he was glad; from what he had, without withholding, he used to give; to the temple he gave tithes; and Maqabis, doing this, rested in good.

1.text: He died, leaving his small sons; and they grew up as their father had ordained for them; they kept the ordinances of their house; they kept all their people; the poor, the widows, and the orphans they did not cause to cry out.

2.text: They feared God; their wealth they gave as alms to the poor; all that their father had committed to them they kept; widows and orphans in their hardship they used to comfort; they used to be father and mother to them; from the hand of those who wronged them they used to deliver them; from any uproar and grief that came upon them they used to comfort them.

1.text: That enemy of God, the arrogant Ṣiruṣaydan, appointed false priests and servants for his idols.

2.text: They used to offer sacrifice to them; they used to pour out wine for them.

3.text: It seemed to him that they ate and drank.

4.text: Each morning he gave them cows and sheep, goats and heifers; morning and evening he offered sacrifice; from that defiled sacrifice he ate.

5.text: Furthermore, he stirred up and compelled others to sacrifice to the idols; it was not only he himself who did it.

6.text: And when the priests of the idols saw the sons of Maqabis — that they were comely and worshiped their Creator God — they desired to lead them astray to sacrifice and to eat of the defiled sacrifice; but those blessed sons of Maqabis refused them.

7.text: For they kept their father’s commandment; in doing good works they stood firm; they utterly feared God. To persuade them to consent was impossible.

8.text: And when they had bound them, and reviled them, and plundered them,

9.text: they reported to King Ṣiruṣaydan that they refused to bow down to the idols and to sacrifice.

10.text: Therefore the king was angry; and grieved; and he commanded that they be brought; they were brought, and stood before him; and he said, “Bow down to the gods; offer sacrifice.”

11.text: They answered: “As for us, we will not turn back to you in this matter; to your defiled idols we will not offer sacrifice.”

12.text: He frightened them with many tortures; but because they had believed in God and steeled their hearts, he could not overcome them.

13.text: Then he kindled fire and cast them in; and they gave their souls to God.

14.text: And after they died, alive once more, holding their drawn swords, they appeared to him by night as he was lying on the throne of his kingdom; and he was utterly afraid.

15.text: And he said to them: “Lords, consent to me! What shall I do for you? All you have commanded me, I will do; do not take my soul.” They utterly terrified him.

16.text: And they said: “Remember that God is your Creator,” telling him all that was fitting. “And there is one who shall remove you from this arrogance and bring you down with your father the Devil to the Gehenna below; there, when we have done you no wrong, while we were worshiping our Creator God, while we were bowing down to him in fear of his Godhead — yet you burned us with fire — you will fulfill all your sentence.

17.text: “For he it is who has created all — heaven and earth, the sea and what is in it,

18.text: “the sun and the moon, the stars, all his creation — he is the LORD.

19.text: “In heaven above and on earth beneath, there is no other God besides him; he is the Almighty; nothing is impossible for him. He kills and saves, scourges and forgives.

20.text: “He rules heaven and earth; there is none who escapes his hand.

21.text: “Except for you, criminal, and the criminals like you whose minds your father Satan has blinded — from all his creation, none transgresses his commandment. You and those idols of yours shall descend together to Gehenna which has no exit forever.

22.text: “It is not you alone who do this; for Satan is your teacher who taught you this evil work, that you might do evil to us.

23.text: “You did not remember God who created you; you make yourself like God your Creator.

24.text: “Until God humbles you, you boast in the work of your hand and in your idols; and for all the sin and iniquity you have done on earth, he will avenge himself against you.”

1.text: “Woe to you and those like you — who do not know God your Creator, who do not keep his commandment and his word! For you are reserved, when you are seized in the affliction of Sheol and scourged, to repent in worthless repentance.

2.text: “To your idols who have neither soul nor breath — who neither avenge those who do evil to them, nor do good to those who do good to them — to whom you and your priests sacrifice and bow down as your Creator God: you have no exit from her [Gehenna] forever.

3.text: “For they are the work of human hands; Satan speaks through them, that he may lead astray the minds of fools like you, that he may bring you and the servants of your gods and the demons who command you down to the fire of Gehenna.

4.text: “You sin and you err; for you do not know that they have no profit for you.

5.text: “Even the cattle and wild beasts and dogs that God created for your food are better than you. For they have no further condemnation beyond one death.

6.text: “But you shall die; and again forever, in Gehenna which has no exit, the grinding [judgment] shall fall upon you.”

7.text: Speaking thus, they went away; from him they vanished.

8.text: But that Ṣiruṣaydan, seized by grievous fear, spent the night trembling; until daybreak it did not leave him.

9.text: After this, he went to the place where he had cast the bodies of the righteous; but he did not find them. For he had wished to bury them. But because God had hidden them, that he might not go and touch their bodies, he found them not.

1.text: He went in pride and the cunning of his heart.

2.text: In his kingdom, as Daniel saw — the strong iron — he encompassed the surrounding countries of the heathen.

3.text: In all foolishness and wickedness, in uproar, he lived.

4.text: What we said before — he breaks, he crushes, he devours.

5.text: As he had stiffened his neck like his father the Devil, who spits out venom, he tramples the remnant under his feet.

6.text: He does not know that God is his Creator; rather, he says: “My days have become like the days of heaven.”

7.text: And in his heart he thinks: “From me the sun rises.”

8.text: He rises in might; in the lot of Zebulun he encamps; in Macedonia he raises battle; from Samaria he receives his food-tribute; from Syria they give him gifts of homage.

9.text: In the districts of the nomads he encamps; he reaches as far as Sidon; in Achaia he lays tribute; to the flowing sea he exalts his neck; returning, he sends his messages even to the Indian Ocean.

1.text: O weak man, you who are not God! Why do you boast? Today you are man; tomorrow you are earth and ashes; in your grave you become worm and rotting.

2.text: Furthermore — Sheol shall follow you and those who do your work. For your teacher is Sebelyanos who, by causing our father Adam to err, brings the sin of the whole world back upon his own head;

3.text: for, by self-exaltation and the hardening of his heart, he refused to bow down to the work of his Creator.

4.text: And you, like your teacher, have refused to bow down to your Creator God.

5.text: You too shall go as those before you went — who did not know God their Creator.

6.text: As they were avenged for the evil work they did on earth, and as they descended to Sheol —

7.text: so also you, like them, shall descend to Gehenna.

8.text: You have stirred his anger. God who gave you authority over the five kingdoms — to worship him you have neglected. Do you think you can escape from God’s hand?

9.text: Whether you do his will or not — he searches you. If on earth you make your way straight, God will prosper your way; all on which you lay your hand he will prosper; he will bless you; your ancient enemies and your daily enemies he will subdue to you.

10.text: In your going-out and your coming-in, in the fruit of your belly, in your flocks and your herds, in the work of your hands that you take in hand, in all your heart imagines, he gladdens you. That you may do thus — that you may work and plant, that you may pull down — authority has been given you from God; all shall obey you.

11.text: But if you refuse to hear God’s word and law, and do not live by his judgment — for all his judgment is truth — there is no escaping from God’s hand, just as those before you, the criminals who did not properly worship God or stand firm in his straight judgment, could not.

12.text: From his presence nothing is hidden; rather, all is utterly revealed before him.

13.text: It is he who holds the authority of kings; it is he who overturns the thrones of the mighty.

14.text: It is he who exalts the humbled; it is he who lifts up the fallen.

15.text: It is he who looses those who are bound; it is he who raises the dead. For from him is the dew of mercy: when he wills, he raises the people whose flesh has decayed and rotted and become as dust.

16.text: Those who have grieved him by doing evil works he also raises — to the resurrection of judgment; he avenges himself against them.

17.text: And on earth he destroys their seed; for they are the ones who broke God’s law and his ordinance.

18.text: For the way of the righteous is harder than the way of the wicked; therefore the wicked do not love to live in the counsel of the righteous.

19.text: As heaven is far from earth, so is the way of the righteous far from the way of the wicked.

20.text: For the way of the wicked is the way of plunder and wickedness, of violence and lechery, of covetousness and denial; it is to grow drunken in violence and to seize the wealth of others.

21.text: It is to run swiftly to shed human blood; to do destruction without benefit; to make the orphan cry out; to eat blood and what is dead-of-itself; to eat the flesh of the camel and the swine; to go in to one in childbed and to a woman in her blood not yet purified.

22.text: All this work of the wicked is the broad way and the laid-out snare of Satan, leading to eternal destruction and punishment.

23.text: But the way of the righteous, which is narrow and slender — it is the way that leads to life, to meekness and humility, to love and peace, to fasting and prayer, to the purity of the flesh; the way of keeping oneself from the unprofitable, from eating what has been struck or has died of itself, from going in to another’s wife, and from lechery.

24.text: Sinful people do all this. The righteous keep themselves from all hated work not commanded in the law, from eating impure food, and from all work God does not love.

25.text: The righteous remove themselves from every way God does not love.

26.text: And he loves them; from all their afflictions he keeps them as entrusted wealth; he saves them.

27.text: But the wicked — Satan rules over them; for [the righteous] keep his law and his ordinance and all he loves.

1.text: As for you, kings and princes — do not walk in the path of Satan; but fear God who created you and has kept you until today.

2.text: Stand firm in the law and commandment of God who rules all.

3.text: When the sons of Israel came to Amalek to inherit the country of the Hittites and Canaanites and Perizzites, Balak the son of Zippor

4.text: said to Balaam: “He whom you have cursed is cursed; he whom you have blessed is blessed. Come and curse them for me; and I will give you much gold and silver that shall honor you.”

5.text: And Balaam, hoping for the wage of his divination, came; and Balak son of Zippor showed him the place where the sons of Israel were encamped.

6.text: He performed his divination; he offered sacrifice; he slaughtered the fattened cows and sheep; he wished to curse the sons of Israel.

7.text: But God did not wish that he curse them. By his word he turned the curse into a blessing.

8.text: And he said: “You are the people God has chosen; you are the dwelling-place of the Beloved who comes from heaven. Let those who bless you be blessed; and those who curse you, cursed.”

9.text: After he had blessed them before him, Balak son of Zippor was grieved; he was utterly angry; he commanded that he curse them.

10.text: And Balaam said: “The people whom God has blessed have come to this country; I will not curse those whom God has blessed.”

11.text: And Balak son of Zippor said to Balaam: “I wished that you curse them for me; but you have not cursed them; before me you have utterly blessed them. If you had cursed them for me and had said, ‘Give to me,’ I would have given you a houseful of gold and silver; but you have utterly blessed them; for me you have done no good; for you I will do no good.”

12.text: And Balaam said: “What word God puts in my mouth, that I will speak; for I cannot disregard the word of God or transgress it.

13.text: “As for me, I do not love wealth more than my soul. If I loved wealth, God would be angry with me — that I should not curse the blessed people.”

14.text: For God had said to their father Jacob: “Those who bless you shall be blessed; those who curse you, cursed.” [Num 24:9 / Gen 27:29]

15.text: Every man who blesses you is blessed; every man who curses you without judgment is cursed. To make God love you, prosper your way and your work.

16.text: Do not be like those before, who grieved God in their wickedness, and whom he disregarded. Some of them he destroyed with the flood of destruction.

17.text: Some of them he destroyed by the hand of their enemies. Bringing the wicked enemies who afflicted them, he captured their kings together with their priests and their prophets.

18.text: They led them into a foreign country they did not know; they utterly led them captive; they scourged them; they destroyed their country.

19.text: They broke down the wall and rampart of the holy city; they made Jerusalem like a field.

20.text: The priests too were taken captive; the law was broken; the warriors fell by the sword.

21.text: Widows were taken captive; for their dead husbands they did not weep; they had been taken captive; they wept for themselves.

22.text: Children wept; elders were shamed; they did not show pity to the face of the elder and the grey-haired.

23.text: To the beautiful, and to those under the law, they showed no pity. All they found in their country they destroyed. When [God] first willed to break down the Temple — because he was angry with his people — they took them captive and led them to a foreign country they did not know.

24.text: Therefore, when God disregarded the sons of Israel, he made Jerusalem to be plowed like a field; for always they grieved their Creator.

25.text: But he did not destroy them at once in any way; for he has mercy for their fathers’ sake, not for their own. For he loves those who reigned in truth, who lived steadfast in straight law before their Creator: their fathers Abraham and Isaac and Jacob.

26.text: And he appointed them to double honor; in heaven and on earth, they received the two-fold kingdom.

27.text: So also you kings and princes who live in this passing world — remember your fathers who lived in fitting work, who served God in good conduct, who inherited the kingdom of heaven, whose name has become beautiful from generation to generation.

28.text: So also, that he may straighten your kingdom, that he may make your name good — make your work straight, like the good kings who served God in good conduct before you.

1.text: Remember Moses the man of God! In his prayer and his meekness, while he kept all this people, he was not vexed; he did not destroy them. But for his brother and his sister — when God had wished to destroy them at once — in his meekness he interceded before God for their sin thus: “O Lord, your people have transgressed before you; forgive your people; do not disregard them.

2.text: “Forgive me, your servant who am a sinner — for I too have transgressed before you. For you are merciful and forgiving; forgive also for them.”

1.text: Woe to you, mighty of Israel, who have not kept what [God] commanded you in the tent, who have done his will except by your own will! And this is — pride and arrogance, lechery and covetousness, drunkenness and drink, swearing in falsehood.

2.text: Therefore my wrath shall burn upon you like the chaff before fire; like the fire that consumes the mountain; like the whirlwind that takes the powdered dust from the earth and scatters it to the heavens so that no trace of its work is found —

3.text: so I will destroy all who work wickedness, says the Holy One of Israel, the LORD. Remember the LORD who rules all; nothing is impossible for him.

4.text: Those who love him, he loves; those who walk in his commandment — their transgression and sin he forgives. Do not be deaf in unbelief and dull of heart.

5.text: Make your minds straight toward God; trust in him that you may save your souls; on the day of your affliction I will save you from the hand of your enemies.

6.text: “And when you call on me, behold I say: I am with you. From the hand of your enemies I will save you; because you have trusted in me, because you have done my commandment, because you have not gone out from my law, because you have loved what I love — on the day of your affliction I will not disregard you,” says the LORD who rules all.

7.text: Those who love him, he loves; for he is compassionate and forgiving; those who keep his commandment, he keeps.

8.text: Many times he turns his wrath from them; because he knows they are flesh and blood, he is forgiving; in all his scourging he does not destroy. When their soul is separated from their flesh, they return to their earth-nature.

9.text: For from non-existence he created them; until God wills again to bring them from non-existence, they do not know the place where they shall dwell; for he has taken their soul; the earth-nature he has returned to its earth-nature.

10.text: Again, by his will, he brings them from non-existence into existence.

11.text: But Ṣiruṣaydan, the denier of God, multiplied arrogance before God’s face; until the day [God] willed [his end] — when [God] forsook him — he exalted himself.

12.text: And he said: “My days have become like the days of heaven. I am the one who brings forth the sun. Until forever, I shall not die.”

13.text: And before he had finished speaking this thing, an angel of death whose name is Ṭelmiyakos descended and struck his heart; in that very hour he died. He had not praised his Creator; through the abundance of his arrogance and the wickedness of his work, he was separated from his beautiful life and perished.

14.text: And the army of the king of the Chaldeans, which had wished to fight him — when it was encamped outside his city and the square of his country — at his death, came out and destroyed his country; they plundered all his cattle; up to the wall they left no man.

15.text: They plundered all his wealth; they took his utensils; they burned his city with fire and returned to their country.

1.text: And those who believed — the five sons of Maqabis — refusing to eat the sacrifice offered to the idol, gave their bodies up to death.

2.text: Knowing that this world grows old and passes, that pleasure does not abide forever — that they might be saved from the fire in heaven, they gave their bodies to fire.

3.text: For they knew that to challenge God is worse than to challenge man; that the wrath of God is worse than the wrath of a king.

4.text: “O Lord, one day’s gladness in Paradise is better than many years’ life on earth; better is one hour of your forgiveness than many years.

5.text: “What are our days as men? Are they not as a passing shadow — like wax beside fire?

6.text: “But you, O Lord, abide forever; your years are not fulfilled; the calling of your name is from generation to generation.”

7.text: And the sons of Maqabis sang this and the like; they chose to trust in God; they refused to eat the defiled sacrifice;

8.text: therefore, knowing that the dead rise and that after the resurrection judgment shall be pronounced, for the sake of God they gave their bodies to martyrdom.

9.text: O people who do not know and do not believe the resurrection of the dead — from these five men, who in their brotherly love gave their bodies up together to death, knowing that their later life is better than this passing earthly life — learn!

10.text: Knowing that all things pass, and because they trusted in him, and did not bow to the idol, and did not eat the dead-of-itself or defiled sacrifice — they gave their bodies up to death, that they might receive praise from God.

11.text: Having wives and children, they did not regard the sweetness of this world or the bitterness of death; knowing that on the last day they will be glad in soul and body, knowing that on the last day the resurrection in soul and body will be done, they gave their bodies up to death.

12.text: Those who kept the ordinance of God — knowing that in the world to come, where there is no sickness or sorrow or death, they shall reign with the good kings and princes who believed God’s word for generation upon generation and for long ages —

13.text: seeing in their hearts what is yet to be, in the midst of the fire as wax they gave their bodies up to death.

14.text: Hoping that their faces shall shine seven times brighter than the sun, that when all are raised in soul and body they shall be glad in his love — they gave their bodies up to death.

1.text: The matter of the Jews and the Samaritans, the Pharisees and the Sadducees, who do not believe the resurrection of the dead — this greatly grieves me; my heart knows it. The Jews say: “Let us eat, let us drink; for tomorrow we die; there is nothing we see beyond.”

2.text: The Samaritans say: “Our flesh becomes dust; therefore it does not rise.

3.text: “At the time of the resurrection, we believe in the rising of our soul. For the soul is invisible like the wind, like a thunder-voice — no one can say, ‘See, here she is’; she is not seen. Therefore even if the flesh dies, she does not die.

4.text: “But our flesh is visible in all; she becomes ash and dust. For wild beasts eat her; worms in the grave eat her.

5.text: “And those who have eaten her become as grass; they become dust as though never created; they become ash; their trace is not found. Where shall the rotten bodies be found?”

6.text: The Pharisees say: “We believe the rising of the dead. But souls — not on earth — in heaven, [God] clothes them with another body.”

7.text: The Sadducees say: “After our soul has gone out from our flesh, we do not rise from death; for soul and body there is no resurrection; after we die, we do not rise.”

8.text: Therefore they utterly err; they speak blasphemy against God and his Lordship; their case grieves me.

9.text: They have not believed in God who justifies them; they have no hope of salvation; nor of rising from the dead.

10.text: O blind Jew! Will you make God who created you from non-existence — who, while you were as spittle, made you man — into one ignorant of knowledge? Is it impossible for him who created you in his image and likeness to unite your soul and your body and raise you?

11.text: You shall not escape from God’s hand; do not think thus. Without your willing, you shall rise. At your death, the cord of Sheol by which you were taken is on your neck; without your willing, you shall be judged.

12.text: For that cord which is bound on your neck — from the stalk of Sheol — sprouts up to you in your mother’s womb. As you grow, she also grows.

13.text: And at your death they place her on your neck; when they pull her stalk, she brings them; she draws her branches.

14.text: All sinners are seized within her with the cord on their neck.

15.text: And the souls of all sinners come from the edge of heaven where they are; so also your cord draws your soul from where you are and brings you into Sheol.

16.text: After your flesh is separated from your soul, like the flesh of our father Adam, in completeness, by God’s grace and dew, it rises. There, as you have done iniquity and sin, as you have not believed, you shall receive your recompense.

17.text: Do not think you only deceive others; you deceive yourself; in your error you abide in the grave; and saying “there is no resurrection of the dead,” you cause [people] to depart from the commandment of God.

18.text: As you have done your work, that he may give you your recompense, he shall raise you. Who, in the dust and ash, will leave you?

19.text: At that time, if there is in you a wind-nature [which is] in the wind, if there is in you a water-nature [which is] in the water, if there is in you an earth-nature [which is] on earth, if there is in you a fire-nature [which is] in fire — it shall come.

20.text: Even the soul that dwelt in you, dwelling in a dark place, shall come.

21.text: And the souls of the righteous, who dwell in joy in Paradise, shall come.

22.text: And you, O Jew, and you, O Samaritan, and you, O Pharisee, and you, O Sadducee — until you are judged, you shall dwell in darkness.

23.text: Then, because you deceived people, as your work was, you shall see how God repays you.

24.text: And you say: “The dead do not rise; tomorrow we die; let us eat and drink” — though you sit on Moses’s seat, in your word you say “there is no resurrection of the dead.”

25.text: Therefore, knowing the book of the Torah and teaching the word of the Scriptures, you err. It would have been better for you had you not learned — [and thus] not deceived people.

26.text: With your evil teaching and your unprofitable word, you cause God’s people to deny [him]. It would have been better had you not known the word of the Scriptures.

27.text: But you — as your work and the fruit of your lips, so shall be given you. For God shows no partiality of face; to his friends who teach good work, he gives from the grace he has prepared.

28.text: And from God who judges you, there is no escape; he will repay you according to your work; you and those you taught shall be judged together.

29.text: And know that the dead rise. Those who kept the law shall also rise; in the grave they cannot remain; for when rain falls, the earth brings forth grass — so his commandment brings them forth.

30.text: As when rain has watered the earth, the moist tree puts forth leaves; as wheat produces grain; as the grain field puts forth shoots; and as God, when he wills, cannot be refused her fruit;

31.text: as a pregnant woman, when birth-pangs have taken her, cannot close her womb or escape without giving birth —

32.text: so the earth — those gathered into her, she brings forth. After she has heard the word of God, she cannot close her womb; for the dew commanded from God descends upon her, and in one time she shall bear them all.

33.text: And the bodies shall be gathered at the places where their corpses fell; and the storehouses of souls shall be opened; and the souls shall return to the flesh from which they were first separated.

34.text: And when the trumpet is sounded, the dead shall rise in the blink of an eye; they shall stand before God; and as their hands’ work, so shall be given them.

35.text: At that time you shall see that you too rise with the dead; you shall marvel at all the work you did on earth; and when you see them written before your eyes, then you shall repent with worthless repentance.

36.text: You shall know that with the dead you rise; and as you have done, so you shall receive.

1.text: Those who find their good work shall be glad at that time. But those who disregarded, saying “the dead do not rise,” when they see that the dead are raised with their useless evil work, then they shall grieve.

2.text: That work they did shall judge them; and they themselves know that they shall be judged without dispute.

3.text: In the day of weeping and judgment — in the day of the final-decree, in the day of the LORD — the godless shall stand in the place of standing.

4.text: In the day of utter darkness, in the day of mist, in the day of lightning, in the day of thunder,

5.text: in the day of fear and trembling, in the day of cold and heat, in the day of frost,

6.text: in the day in which the evil man receives his recompense as he did evil; in the day in which the pure man receives his wage as he did pure work; in the day in which the sinner receives his recompense as he did sin;

7.text: in the day in which the master is not honored above his servant, when the mistress is not honored above her maidservant,

8.text: when the king is not honored above the poor, when the elder is not honored above the child, when the father is not honored above the son, when the mother is not honored above the daughter,

9.text: when the rich is not honored above the poor, when the arrogant is not honored above the humbled, when the great is not honored above the small. For it is the day of judgment; the day of recompense and punishment; the day in which each receives as he has done.

10.text: It is the day in which those who did good works receive their wage; the day in which those who did evil receive evil.

11.text: It is the day in which those who received their wage are glad; the day in which those who received evil grieve. And those who twist the Scriptures, saying “the dead do not rise,” also see.

12.text: Then the sinners of the earth weep for the sin they have done; and for the unsettled grief that comes upon them because of their failure to do good while on earth.

13.text: Likewise, because they did good work on earth, the joy of the doers of good — the good — shall not be fulfilled forever.

14.text: Knowing that they shall rise from death, they did not depart from the law of their Creator.

15.text: Because they did not depart from his commandment, they shall inherit two lives; on earth he multiplied their seed; he blessed their children.

16.text: And in heaven, on the day of resurrection — when the rich become poor — he shall give them as inheritance the Kingdom of Heaven, which he swore to their fathers.

17.text: Those who do evil and do not believe the rising of the dead, who do not consider the law of God and the day of resurrection — they shall weep.

18.text: Then they shall see the affliction without end, the affliction without salvation or settlement that comes upon them; in their mind there shall be unsettled grief without rest.

19.text: The worm that does not sleep, the fire that is not quenched, shall reach them.

20.text: And on the place where their flesh is, fire and sulphur, whirlwind, frost and hail, brimstone shall rain upon them.

21.text: Upon the people who do not believe the rising of the dead is the fire of Gehenna.

1.text: Consider for yourself what is in your flesh: the nails of your hands and feet, and the hair of your head. When you cut them, they grow swiftly back. If you have heart and mind to believe, know this from that.

2.text: From where do these — the nails of your hand and foot, and the hair of your head — come, you ask? Has not God prepared them to grow, that you may know the resurrection in your own flesh, not in another’s — that you may know the resurrection done in you?

3.text: And you, saying “there is no resurrection of the dead,” deceiving people — as you have done sin and iniquity, you shall receive your recompense at the time of the resurrection.

4.text: When the day of your recompense reaches you, you shall see it. Even the wheat, even the barley you have sown does not refuse to sprout.

5.text: Again — the plant you planted does not say “I will not sprout”; whether vine or fig, the leaf and the fruit do not change.

6.text: If you plant a vine, it does not change to become a fig; if you plant a fig, it does not change to become a vine; if you sow wheat, it does not change to become barley;

7.text: if you sow barley, it does not change to become wheat. Rather, all by their kind and clan, by their fruit and tree, by their leaf and root — receiving blessing through the dew of mercy from God — bring forth fruit.

8.text: So also the earth — what God sowed in her, soul and flesh, she brings forth; what God sowed, soul and flesh in unity, shall rise. Those who did good works are not exchanged for those who did evil; those who did evil are not exchanged for those who did good.

9.text: When the hour of the trumpet’s sounding has come, the dead shall rise by the dew of mercy from God; those who did good shall rise to the resurrection of life; their wage is what God has prepared for the good — the dwelling of the pure, the Paradise of joy, where there is no affliction or disease, where they shall no more die.

10.text: But those who did evil shall rise to the resurrection of judgment, and with the deceiver Devil,

11.text: with his armies the demons — who do not wish that even one of the sons of men should be saved — they shall go to eternal punishment.

12.text: To the edge of darkness where there is grinding of teeth and weeping; where there is no forgiveness or mercy; where there is no exit forever — they shall descend into Gehenna. While they were in their flesh, on earth in their life, they did no good work.

13.text: Therefore both soul and flesh shall be judged at the resurrection.

14.text: Woe to those who do not believe the rising of soul and flesh in unity — by which God shows the multitude of his wonders!

15.text: All — each one — shall receive his wage as his work and the labor of his hand.

1.text: A grain of wheat does not sprout if it does not first break; it bears no fruit. But if the wheat-grain breaks, it sends down its root to the earth; it puts forth a leaf; it becomes a shoot; it bears fruit.

2.text: You know that one grain of wheat becomes many grains.

3.text: Likewise, this grain sprouts because of wind and water and earth; the sun stands in place of fire. Wheat cannot bear fruit without the sun.

4.text: The wind stands in place of the soul; without the wind, wheat cannot bear; the water gives the earth drink and quenches her thirst.

5.text: The earth, after she has drunk the water, brings forth the root; her shoot ascends; as God has blessed her, she bears.

6.text: But the grain of wheat is the image of Adam, in which the rational soul God created has dwelt; so also the vine — it drinks water; it sends down its root; the slender cords of its root pull water.

7.text: And it raises that water to the tips of its leaves; for the dew from God waters the tall tips of the vines. In the heat of the sun, it sprouts forth; by the will of God, it bears fruit.

8.text: It makes a sweet savor that gladdens the heart; when one eats, it satisfies like grain that does not let one hunger, like water that does not let one thirst; when pressed, it becomes wine.

9.text: When drunk, it gladdens the heart of man — “wine gladdens the heart of man,” as said in the Psalm. The careless man who opens his mouth and drinks becomes drunk; it fills his lungs; the blood flows to his heart.

10.text: Wine intoxication greatly deceives, taking his sense; the ditch and the cliff he sees as a wide field; he does not know the stumbling-block and thorn at his hand and foot.

11.text: And God did so with the vine and its fruit — that he might be praised in his name by those who do his will and believe the resurrection of the dead.

12.text: Those who believe the rising of the dead — he gladdens in the dwelling of life.

1.text: People who do not believe the resurrection of the dead — how greatly do you err? When they have led you to a place you do not know, when they have cast you into Gehenna because you did not believe the rising of the dead in soul and body together, then you shall repent with useless repentance.

2.text: Saying “we know the dead, who have become dust and ash, do not rise,” you deceive the minds of your neighbors — and you shall receive your wage as you have done, whether good or evil.

3.text: Therefore they deceive their neighbors. Their death has no rest; their scourge has no strength; in their toil they have not stood firm; before God’s assize they must stand.

4.text: When [God] rebukes them in his wrath, when he is angry that they have done evil, they shall be greatly ashamed. They speak without knowing the way of God; they do not know where they came from.

5.text: Nor the Gehenna they go to do they know; full of wrath, perverse in their work and evil, they teach their neighbors according to the perversity of their mind. Saying “there is no resurrection of the dead,” they teach a perverse thing.

6.text: Then they shall know the dead rise; that they shall be judged because they did not believe the resurrection of the dead that comes for all the kindred of the sons of men.

7.text: For we are all sons of Adam; and by Adam we have died. By the transgression of our father Adam, we have received the sentence of death from God.

8.text: Again, that we may receive our wages for the work we have done, we shall rise with our father Adam; for by our father Adam’s ignorance, the world was subjected to death.

9.text: Therefore, by Adam’s transgression, we receive our recompense. Our flesh melts in the grave; our bones are crushed.

10.text: The earth drinks our marrow; we perish; the beauty of our face perishes in the dust; our flesh is buried in the tomb; our beautiful voice is buried in the earth.

11.text: From our shining eyes, worms come forth; our form perishes in the grave; we become dust.

12.text: Where is the beauty of the youths whose form was beautiful, whose stature was lovely, whose speech was smooth?

13.text: Where is the strength of warriors? Where is the might of kings, the honor of princes? Where is the parading on horseback, the adornment in gold and silver, the parading in shining weapons?

14.text: Where is the taste of dainty foods and the sweet drinking of wine?

1.text: O Earth, who have gathered kings and princes, the great and the honored, lovely women and fair maidens — woe to you because of yourself!

2.text: Those of good form, fair of countenance, possessed of knowledge and mind — whose word, like the playing of the harp, like the song of the lyre and the lute, was beautiful in melody;

3.text: whose voice, like sweet wine, gladdened; whose eyes shone like the morning star;

4.text: whose right hand was strong to give and take, who shot arrows; whose feet, like even wheels, ran beautifully — mighty men whom you have gathered — O Earth, woe to you because of yourself!

5.text: O Death, sent by the will of God, who has separated the souls of beautiful people from their flesh — woe to you because of yourself!

6.text: And you also, Earth! You have gathered the many bodies which God brought forth from you and returned to you. Woe to you because of yourself! By the will of God we came forth from you; to you we return; by the will of God we were glad upon you.

7.text: You became a couch for our corpses; on you we walked; in you we lay down; we ate your fruit; you ate our flesh.

8.text: From your spring, water we drank; you drank from the spring of our blood; from your fatness of earth we ate; you ate the fatness of our bones.

9.text: From your earth — that you might be our food, as God commanded — full of dew, grain we ate; you received the beauty of our flesh; as God commanded you, you made it dust for your food.

10.text: O Death, you who have gathered many mighty kings and princes — who, as God who created you commanded, were not afraid of their splendor and majesty, who did not despise even the hungry — woe to you because of yourself!

11.text: You have not pitied those of fair countenance; you have not left the strong and the warriors; the rich and the poor, the ill-favored and the fair, elders and children, women and men — you have not left.

12.text: Those who thought good and did not transgress his commandment, you have not left; those who in their work were as beasts, who thought evil, you have not left. Those whose beauty was perfect, whose word and matter were sweet, you have not left.

13.text: Those whose word was wrathful and whose mouth was full of curse, you have not left; their souls you gathered into your storehouses of light and darkness.

14.text: And the earth — gathered their flesh, whether in cave or in earth — until the trumpet is sounded and the dead rise.

15.text: Those who did evil shall receive their wage as their work. For at the sound of the trumpet and the commandment of God, the dead rise in the blink of an eye; and those who did good works shall be glad.

1.text: When in fear and trembling we stand before him, believe me — all the work we have done on earth shall not be hidden or pass away.

2.text: When we shall not have provisions for the way; when we shall have no garment for our body;

3.text: when we shall have no staff for our hand and no sandals for our feet;

4.text: when there shall be mire, ravine, darkness, thorn and bramble, sea-depth, pit-depth — when we do not know the way they take us;

5.text: when we do not know those who take us — and do not hear their speech;

6.text: for they are dark and lead us to darkness; we do not see their face.

7.text: As the prophet David said: “When my soul was failing within me, O LORD my God, you knew my path; in the way I walked, they hid a snare against me. I looked to my right, and saw; there was no one who knew me; there was no place of refuge for me.” [Ps 142:3–4]

8.text: And David, when he said this, knew that the demons mock him and lead him to a way he does not know. Turning to the right and to the left, he found no one who knew him.

9.text: None knew him; but he was in the midst of the angels of darkness.

10.text: Those sent to the righteous are subtle angels of light, who receive the souls of the righteous and lead them to the place of life and light.

11.text: But those sent to the souls of the wicked are angels of darkness and demons, who take them and lead them to the eternal punishment prepared for them — that they may receive their recompense for the sin they have done.

12.text: Those who lead them to destruction — woe to the souls of the wicked, who have no rest or escape, who have no exit forever from the affliction that has come upon them.

13.text: They have gone in the way of Cain; they have perished in the iniquity of Balaam; they have abandoned all they ought to have done. To take by violence the wealth of another that is not theirs, they justify the taking of bribes and usury.

14.text: And as their work has been, so shall they receive their recompense in the fire of Gehenna.

1.text: Where are those people who in violence gathered the wealth of others — wealth not their own, not the work of their own hand?

2.text: Without payment they take the wealth of others; not knowing the day of their death that shall reach them, they gather; and to strangers they leave their wealth.

3.text: Their children do not rejoice in their fathers’ wealth; for like their fathers — sinners who afflict and seize, whether by theft or by plunder — they are the kindred of the wicked.

4.text: Their fathers’ wealth does not profit them; it has been gathered by plunder and violence. Like the mist of urine, like the smoke the wind scatters, like the grass that withers, like the wax that melts before fire — so shall the honor of the wicked perish.

5.text: As David said: “I saw the sinner like the cedar of Lebanon, flourishing and exalted; but when I returned, I missed him; I sought him; I did not find his place.” [Ps 37:35–36]

6.text: That those who today wrong their neighbors — gathering by violence the wealth of others, thinking themselves immortal — may not boast: the destruction of the wicked is thus, in one moment.

7.text: O fools — consider that you pass away, and that your wealth passes with you. Your gold and silver, however much, shall become rust.

8.text: Though you multiply children, it shall be the multiplication of graves; though you multiply houses, they shall be in ruin.

9.text: Because you have not done the will of God your God, though you multiply cattle, they shall become plunder for your enemies; for they are not blessed; all the wealth on which you have laid your hand shall not be found.

10.text: Whether in house or in wilderness, whether in pasture or in field, whether in threshing-floor or in winepress — it shall not be found.

11.text: Even in the fruit of your belly you shall not rejoice; rather, because of your enemies, it shall be sorrow to you. For because you have not kept the commandment of God, God will not save you together with all your household.

12.text: But those who have kept his law, ordinance, and commandment — from his blessing he does not withhold; all they have asked he gives; the fruit of their land and the fruit of their belly he blesses.

13.text: That they may rule and not be ruled, he sets them above all the heathen surrounding them; in their pasture-place he gives them all his blessing.

14.text: All on which they lay their hand, all the fruit of their field, all the place of their cattle, he blesses; in the fruit of their belly he gladdens them.

15.text: He does not diminish their cattle; from all their afflictions — from sickness and weariness, from destruction, from what is known and unknown — he saves them.

16.text: In the time of judgment he contends for them; from evil and affliction, from all who oppose them, he saves them. In the beginning, the Levite who received the work of the tent as a trust kept the work of the tent; if he walked in the will of God, in the first law as in all the [later] law, they gave him the tithe and the firstborn from man to cattle.

17.text: As Moses commanded Joshua the son of Nun, in their cities was a city of refuge — that any man might be saved there who had killed another, whether knowing or unknowing, until those who judge and those who are judged gave judgment.

18.text: “Examine in your mind whether he had a previous quarrel with him,” he said to them;

19.text: “and whether by axe, or stone, or wood — if it fell from his hand unknowingly and the man on whom it fell died — examining, save him; he did it unknowingly; he shall be saved.

20.text: “But if he did it knowingly, as his trespass deserves he shall receive his recompense; there is none who shows him mercy. If he did it unknowingly and killed him — because he did it unknowingly, examining, save him that he may not die.”

21.text: Moses had made for the sons of Israel an ordinance such as this, that they might not transgress the commandment of God; he had made for them an ordinance that they might depart from all wickedness.

22.text: That they might live by his judgment and his law — that they might wholly keep themselves from worshiping idols, from eating dead-of-itself and paw-struck — for those who live in the commandment of God and depart from every evil work, as he had ordained for them — that they might keep themselves utterly from all that is unfitting for the sons of men — he commanded them.

23.text: That they might save their souls, that they might find their dwelling with their fathers who did good — that they might not depart from the commandment he had made for them, in the image of the tent in heaven, he commanded them.

24.text: Those who believe the word of God and walk in his commandment — they are called sons of the righteous. From Adam and Seth, who did the will of God, they are.

25.text: We are sons of Adam; that we should do good work and all that pleases God — for he created us in his image and likeness — he does not despise us.

26.text: If we do good work, with those who did good work we shall inherit the Kingdom of Heaven; for he does not separate those who love each other.

27.text: Those who petition him in purity, he greatly loves; he hears their prayer; those who utterly repent, he accepts their repentance; to people who keep his law and ordinance and commandment, he gives strength and firmness.

28.text: And those who do his will — forever in his Kingdom they shall be glad with him; whether first or last, they shall offer him praise. From today and unto eternity. Amen.
